metadata.principle: Ordered by utility: the grammar you use in the highest share of everyday sentences comes first. Teach a rule only when the learner has met words that need it.
metadata.levels: CEFR band is the level by which this rule should be solid, not a gate — a frequency-first learner meets most A-level grammar in the first weeks.
metadata.note: The tutor introduces the next unmastered rule whose prerequisites are met, drills it in context, and logs it to mastery-db + spaced-repetition just like vocabulary.

rules.name: Subject pronouns (io, tu, lui/lei, noi, voi, loro)
rules.why: Referenced by every conjugated verb; often dropped, so learners must recognize person from the verb.

rules.name: essere (to be) — present tense
rules.why: Most frequent verb; identity, location, description.

rules.name: avere (to have) — present tense
rules.why: Second most frequent verb; possession + builds the passato prossimo.

rules.name: Definite articles (il, lo, la, l', i, gli, le)
rules.why: Every noun takes one; encodes gender + number.

rules.name: Indefinite articles (un, uno, una, un')
rules.why: 'a/an'; needed the moment you name any single thing.

rules.name: Noun gender & plural formation (-o/-i, -a/-e, -e/-i)
rules.why: Drives article and adjective agreement across the whole language.

rules.name: Regular -are verbs — present (parlare)
rules.why: Largest verb class; unlocks hundreds of common verbs.

rules.name: Regular -ere / -ire verbs — present (credere, dormire, capire)
rules.why: Covers the remaining regular verbs, incl. -isc- (capisco).

rules.name: Adjective agreement & position
rules.why: Adjectives match gender+number; most follow the noun.

rules.name: Basic prepositions (di, a, da, in, con, su, per, tra/fra)
rules.why: Glue of every sentence; extremely high frequency.

rules.name: Articulated prepositions (del, al, dalla, nel, sul...)
rules.why: Preposition + article fuse constantly (di+il=del).

rules.name: Yes/no questions & negation (non)
rules.why: Word order barely changes; 'non' before the verb negates it.

rules.name: Question words (chi, cosa, dove, quando, come, perché, quanto)
rules.why: Needed to ask for any information.

rules.name: c'è / ci sono (there is / there are)
rules.why: Existence and availability — everyday staple.

rules.name: Possessive adjectives (il mio, la tua, i suoi...)
rules.why: Take an article in Italian; high frequency.

rules.name: Common irregular present verbs (andare, fare, stare, dare, venire, potere, volere, dovere, sapere, dire)
rules.why: The most-used verbs are irregular; must be memorized early.

rules.name: Passato prossimo (avere/essere + past participle)
rules.why: The default past tense in speech; agreement with essere.

rules.name: Reflexive verbs (mi chiamo, si alza...)
rules.why: Daily-routine verbs; changes auxiliary to essere in the past.

rules.name: Direct object pronouns (lo, la, li, le, mi, ti, ci, vi)
rules.why: Avoids repeating nouns; affects participle agreement.

rules.name: Indirect object pronouns (mi, ti, gli, le, ci, vi)
rules.why: 'to/for someone'; core of verbs like piacere.

rules.name: piacere (to like) construction
rules.why: Inverted structure (mi piace) trips every learner; very frequent.

rules.name: Future tense (parlerò, sarò...)
rules.why: Plans and predictions; also common for probability.

rules.name: Imperfetto (ongoing/habitual past)
rules.why: Pairs with passato prossimo to narrate the past correctly.

rules.name: Imperative (commands: guarda!, senta, andiamo)
rules.why: Directions, instructions, requests; formal vs informal forms.

rules.name: Comparatives & superlatives (più/meno... di/che, il più)
rules.why: Everyday comparison of people, things, options.

rules.name: Particles ne and ci
rules.why: High-frequency, low-transparency; needed to sound natural.

rules.name: Conditional (vorrei, potrei...)
rules.why: Politeness and hypotheticals; 'vorrei' is essential courtesy.

rules.name: Present subjunctive (penso che sia...)
rules.why: Opinion, doubt, emotion; marks educated speech.

rules.name: Relative pronouns (che, cui, il quale)
rules.why: Combines clauses into complex sentences.

rules.name: Hypothetical sentences (se + condizionale/congiuntivo)
rules.why: 'If I were... I would...' — real conversational range.
